_readme: SETUP BUNDLE TEMPLATE — copy this to 'bootstrap.json' (which is gitignored) next
to a fresh WebAgent clone to preconfigure it on first boot. Fill in only the
sections you want; delete the rest. On first boot, if this install has no LLM
configured yet, the app applies these sections (activating the database) and
then renames the file to bootstrap.applied.json. Delete every '_'-prefixed key
before use — they are comments, not config.
TWO WAYS TO SHIP THIS FILE:
1. PLAINTEXT (this template) — you secure the file yourself; no password needed.
2. ENCRYPTED — instead of this JSON, put a single 'WABOOT1....' code string as
the whole file contents (generate it from a running install's Data Settings
> Deployment > 'This app' > Create setup code). Then set the environment
variable BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD to the source admin password so the app
The easiest path is NOT to hand-edit this at all: on a configured install open
Data Settings > Deployment > 'This app' > Create setup code, and paste the code
on the new install's setup page (or save it as bootstrap.json).

admin._comment: The admin login created on the fresh install.

llm._comment: AI provider + preset default model + the saved-model roster. api_key is the real key.

database._comment: App database connection. For SQLite this can be omitted entirely (the app self-creates one).

vault._comment: Secrets-vault backend. 'inline_db' (app DB) or 'os_keyring' need no config; remote vaults take a config object (and their access token is re-entered on the new device).
